bull.b: Very low leverage reduces near-term balance-sheet risk and limits the burden of interest or refinancing obligations. This gives Tenaya greater flexibility to direct available capital toward clinical development and preserves resilience while its pipeline remains pre-commercial.

A pipeline spanning gene therapy, cell therapy, and small molecules gives Tenaya multiple avenues to address cardiovascular disease and underlying mechanisms. This breadth can support portfolio diversification and improve the company’s ability to pursue differentiated clinical opportunities over time.

Adding a CFO can strengthen financial oversight and capital planning during a period of substantial research spending and external financing needs. Better financial leadership may improve resource allocation and help manage the funding strategy required to advance clinical programs.

bear.b: Large and continuing operating losses show that Tenaya remains far from sustainable profitability and must fund substantial investment before commercial products generate meaningful earnings. This weak earnings base can constrain strategic flexibility and increase reliance on future financing.

Negative operating and free cash flow indicates that the business currently consumes cash rather than generating internal funding. Although annual operating cash burn improved from 2022 to 2025, the still-negative TTM figures leave continued dependence on capital access to support development.

bear.t: Eroding capital base and dilution risk
bear.b: The substantial decline in equity reflects the cumulative effect of ongoing losses and weakens the capital base available to support development. Potential dilution from an expanded equity incentive plan could further reduce existing holders’ ownership as the company funds operations and retains talent.
